text: CHAPTER 37
speaker: Narrator

text: The Choice Already Made
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: The knocking came again from somewhere ahead of them, three measured blows traveling through the dark with enough force to tremble beneath Zik's boots. It did not sound nearer than before. The passage had changed direction beneath his hand, bending away from the chamber where the fourth place waited, yet the sound continued to arrive from directly in front of them, as though the City had moved its source to remain useful. Balag lifted the torch and peered into the narrow turn.
speaker: Narrator

text: Its light showed damp stone, a low ceiling, and nothing that might possess knuckles. Behind them, the journal remained open to the same line.
speaker: Narrator

text: THE FOURTH PLACE IS YOURS.
speaker: Narrator
note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

text: The page beneath it was blank.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik closed the cover before it could add anything else. The leather resisted for an instant, not enough to stop him but enough to make the action feel noticed. He tucked the journal beneath his arm and followed Balag into the new passage, leaving Ninsun and Enhedu to fall in behind them. No one suggested another direction. The darkness that had swallowed the chamber had withdrawn only from this route, and even Balag's suspicion had limits when the alternative was walking into a wall they could no longer see.
speaker: Narrator

text: The corridor descended at a shallow angle. Moisture shone in the seams of the stone, gathering into threads that slipped downward beside them and vanished beneath fitted floor slabs. The walls breathed more faintly here, their movement difficult to distinguish from the tremor left by the knocking. Zik kept his left hand against the rock as they walked. Each expansion pressed cool stone into his palm; each contraction left a thin space between skin and wall. The rhythm was irregular, unlike the long, deep respirations they had felt elsewhere in the City.
speaker: Narrator

text: It reminded him of someone attempting to remain quiet while in pain.
speaker: Narrator

text: They had gone no more than thirty paces when Ninsun stopped.
speaker: Narrator

text: Her boots made no sound beyond the scrape of grit under one heel, yet the interruption passed through the group at once. Enhedu nearly walked into her. Balag took two more steps before noticing the torchlight no longer followed, then turned with the expression of a man prepared to dislike whatever came next.
speaker: Narrator

text: We need to return to the wall,
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Balag stared at her for several seconds.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: No.
speaker: Balag

text: You can remain here.
speaker: Ninsun

text: That wasn't permission for the rest of you.
speaker: Balag

text: She shifted the strap of her satchel higher on her shoulder, still studying the darkness behind them.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We accepted the inscription too quickly.
speaker: Ninsun

text: We did not accept it. We left it. That is the opposite of accepting.
speaker: Balag

text: The City gave us a statement. We argued about its meaning, became frightened by its timing, and moved in the direction it provided. That is acceptance in every way that matters.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Enhedu leaned one shoulder against the wall, careful to move with its shallow rise and fall.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: What did we miss?
speaker: Enhedu
note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

text: I don't know yet.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Balag let out a quiet breath through his nose.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Those words have become more dangerous than the knocking.
speaker: Balag

text: Ninsun finally faced them. Dust had settled in the folds of her clothes and along the loose strands of hair near her temple. Fatigue showed in the stiffness of her shoulders, but her attention had sharpened since leaving the chamber. Zik recognized the change. It was the same look she wore when a familiar translation produced an impossible date or when two fragments that should have belonged together refused to meet along the break. Uncertainty did not weaken her. It offended her into precision.
speaker: Narrator

text: The first three marks were already there,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said.
speaker: Narrator

text: The fourth appeared after Zik approached the wall. We assumed that made it the next mark in the sequence.
speaker: Ninsun

text: It was above the others,
speaker: Balag

text: Balag replied.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: It looked unfinished. The journal called it his place. There wasn't much assumption required.
speaker: Balag

text: There was enough.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun took the torch from him before he could object and held it low, illuminating the floor between them.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Did any of you hear stone being cut?
speaker: Ninsun

text: The corridor quieted around the question. Water moved somewhere inside the wall with a thin, dragging sound. Zik searched his memory again, trying to separate what he had witnessed from what the completed shape had taught him to imagine. He remembered Ninsun reading the older carvings, the pressure building behind his eyes, the pale line extending downward. What he could not remember was the sound that should have accompanied it.
speaker: Narrator

text: No,
speaker: Enhedu
